comments.text: It's just like how I felt playing dead rails, game is very fun if you play with friends but when you start going to the late game it gets extremely boring

comments.author: user209
comments.text: I dont think the game is easy for the average player, especially people who never played it, but the lack of a true ending and actual lore is quite disapointing to me

comments.author: user210
comments.text: The issue with 99 nights is after the first fifty days if you know what you're doing you're probably done everything the game has to offer. You've likely went through the cultist hideout, fully upgraded the fire and gotten the best loot so from there it is literally just waiting, maybe occasionally going out to get a bit more resources but even then if you just set up a crock pot and a farm you never have to worry about food.

comments.text: IIRC, I think 99 Nights was made by the same guy/group who were behind the two Break In games that popped off on user134 years ago.

comments.author: user212
comments.text:
From what ive played of it, 99 nights is somewhat boring once you get to a certain point, but there's always the risk of dying when you go for the longer nights.

my cousin and I have consistently been trying to make it to 500 nights with absurd restrictions like only hunting for food (so no camping at the fire with vegetable meals) and no using any classes.

it can get really difficult if you set yourself some limits, and I really think that a challenge mode would make this game a proper good game.

Up hunger drainage, up enemy damage and health, make the deer recover from your lights quicker and when it's hungry, be completely unaffected by your light at all.

Most nights you can literally just run circles around the enemies or sit in a place where they simply cant spawn or get you, so I think a challenge would do this game wonders.
